author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Saudi Arabia said drones launched from Iraq struck its East-West oil pipeline on Friday, adding another flashpoint to a widening regional conflict. The Saudi foreign ministry announced the attack late Friday without immediately detailing the extent of the damage.

Riyadh said it would not retaliate for now after a request from Iraq's prime minister. The kingdom nevertheless reserved the right to take measures it considers necessary to protect its sovereignty, security and critical facilities. The East-West pipeline carries crude from eastern production areas toward the Red Sea, making it an important alternative route when shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is disrupted.

The announcement came amid attacks affecting energy and shipping infrastructure across the Gulf and Red Sea region. Any sustained interruption to the Saudi pipeline could further complicate oil exports, but authorities had not immediately provided operating or flow data. The source of the drones and responsibility for the attack remained subject to investigation. The situation was developing Friday evening, with attention focused on damage assessments and whether diplomatic efforts can prevent a direct Saudi response.
dek: Riyadh said it would hold off on retaliation after a request from Iraq's prime minister while reserving the right to protect critical facilities.
headline: Saudi Arabia says Iraq-launched drones hit East-West pipeline
